<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f97fce35b5f453e6081fcf3ef20534714a64c95` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ab88ab8e34481938371e2b7d333472b134c0d2d7` — the merge of head `f8da2ea030a5d9563ccf82ed873edaa0a5dd2de4` into base `1f97fce35b5f453e6081fcf3ef20534714a64c95`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ab88ab8e34481938371e2b7d333472b134c0d2d7 && git checkout ab88ab8e34481938371e2b7d333472b134c0d2d7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1f97fce35b5f453e6081fcf3ef20534714a64c95 f8da2ea030a5d9563ccf82ed873edaa0a5dd2de4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1f97fce35b5f453e6081fcf3ef20534714a64c95 && git merge --no-ff f8da2ea030a5d9563ccf82ed873edaa0a5dd2de4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f97fce35b5f453e6081fcf3ef20534714a64c95
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 — L1 REWORK @ `245dbd0390b113f7b427e62bddfc618ca08e3c24`

**Verdict: REWORK** (one must-fix in the publish door; everything else below reads clean or is owed later).

### R1 (must-fix) — the per-item publish now refuses a promotion that writes a package-BOUND row

The new guard in `promoteDraftForPublish` asks the disabled-holders judgment whenever `active.unbound || address.drafts.unbound`, whatever the promotion's own address is. Where the only draft is bound to the (disabled) holder and a package-less row is stored, `packagelessDraftAddress` resolves `key = into = PKG` (`unboundItemDraftAddress`: one bound draft candidate), so the promotion reads PKG's draft and writes PKG's active row; it never touches the hidden package-less row. The guard still fires on `active.unbound` and answers the customization refusal, whose sentence says the package-less row is what it protects.

Measured with a local probe in the served-stack fixture of `disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts` (not committed): package-less `fr-FR` row saved, then `saveMetaItem({ packageId: PKG, mode: 'draft', fr-FR })`, `disablePackage(PKG)`, `publishMetaItem({ member: 'fr-FR' })` with no `packageId`.

- Rows before the publish, both runs: `[["active",null,"fr-FR"],["draft","com.acme.mail","fr-FR"]]`.
- Merge base `56c9cae6` (the three `metadata-protocol` src files checked out from it, package rebuilt): `success: true`, "Published draft", rows after `[["active",null,"fr-FR"],["active","com.acme.mail","fr-FR"]]` (the package-less row untouched).
- Head `245dbd0390`: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, "Enable the package that holds email_template 'acme.welcome' first, then send this publish again … Every package holding the name is disabled, and the row stored for it under no …", nothing written.
- Same run: the PR's own file `Tests 9 passed (9)` with the probe, so the existing pins do not see this cell.

Why it is a must-fix, read against the PR's own words: the Acceptance notes bound the change to the customization cell and keep "a write into a package-bound row" out because it "would move a shipped answer beyond the ruled cell". This cell is that write, and its answer moved (`200` → `409`). The changeset's "Every moved answer, before → after" list does not carry it either, so its completeness claim is false at this head. The rollback door does not have this hole: it asks only when `rollbackPackageId === null`, i.e. when the restore writes the package-unbound row.

Fix direction (the dev's call, measured either way): ask the judgment only where the promotion reads a package-less draft or writes the package-less row, i.e. `address.drafts.unbound` for the draft side, and `active.unbound` only when `promoteInto === null`. Add a pin for this cell asserting the merge-base answer (promoted into PKG's row, package-less row byte-identical), with an ablation of the new condition.

### Read and clean at this head

- Shape (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37818`): open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #37608`; the card's Expected is the two doors plus a pin per door, which the diff delivers, so `Fixes` is right. No closing keyword near another open card. No `content/docs/releases/` path.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the same on the changeset. `Skills-docs: none` holds: the changed behaviour is a refusal whose own sentence names the remedy, and no `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` page teaches a bare publish or rollback over a disabled holder.
- `l1-face` changeset flag on `@objectstack/objectql`: a false positive. The only objectql file is `src/*.test.ts`; `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts` and `files[]` is `dist`, so nothing objectql ships moves.
- Published surface: `@objectstack/spec` ships the migration entry through `dist` and `protocol-upgrade-guide.md`; it and `metadata-protocol` are on the changeset (`minor`, BREAKING, ADR-0087 `not-required (already-registered …)`, which matches the entry existing on the merge base).
- Rejection pins assert `status` + `code` (409 / `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`), the remedy's first words, no package named, every stored row byte-identical, then a re-enable control. Reach on main and one ablation per door are written in the body.
- Floor checks at this head: Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`.

### Changeset sentences read (not delegated)

- `.changeset/37608-…`: the BREAKING paragraph, the "did not ask that judgment" paragraph, the three moved-answer bullets and the "Not moved" paragraph, each read against the diff. False at this head: the moved list's completeness (R1). Everything else matches the code.
- `.changeset/37499-…` (DELIBERATE CORRECTION): before "there only the draft discard moves, from `200` to the `409` above."; after "there only the draft discard moves: over a stored package-less draft from `200` to the `409` above, and over a stored package-less row with no draft from the `409` with the `?package=` sentence to the same `409` with the enable sentence." The new sentence matches N11 in card comment 7199079202. Not measured here.

### Owed at the next head (not REWORK reasons)

- `Check Changeset` red: the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class of `check-empty-changeset`. This diff changes code, so the confirmation is a same-head at-tier contract-review PASS that judges the rewritten 37499 sentence (landing-operations). The seat records it on that head.
- Contract review: owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (narrowing face, plus `packages/spec/src/**`). Not started on this head because R1 moves it; this thread runs it isolated on the reworked head.
- ADR-0150 D3 note: the body keeps the stale "Card #37608 carries both doors. Until it lands …" bullet and N11's ADR half out of this PR (Tier H) with "Carrier: the seat". The card's third Expected bullet reads on that note, so the seat files the follow-up and the body names it as `#N` before ACCEPT.
- Dogfood: owed (`!` plus narrowing). No `dogfood_battery` reading for this head is on the card or the PR yet. NOT MEASURED.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `35ca5027ddb57d487ac5e01a859f9d94dbd4e657`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/objectql/src/disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.disabled-holder-package-less-row-bare-write-refused.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-version-gates.ts (`packagelessDraftAddress`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts (`packagelessAddress`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-slots.ts (`historySlotOf`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`restoreVersion`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts (the draft discard's judgment), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-door-requests.ts (`PublishMetaItemRequest.packageId`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts (the publish route's conditional spread), docs/adr/0150 D3's 2026-11-26 note on `main`; and the two changesets, read for ② and for the DELIBERATE CORRECTION sentence

Inputs: card #37608 body and its six comments (7196921497, 7199079202, 7208988317, 7209392169, 7212020709, 7212050411), PR #37818 body and seven-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `56c9cae6`), and the 73 check-runs on this head. Every check-run is `completed`; none is pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Per-item publish naming no package** (`promoteDraftForPublish`): narrower by one cell. Where the request carries no `packageId` key, the draft address is a stored draft with `key` or `into` null, and every holder of the name is disabled, it answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (`disabledHoldersCustomizationRefusal`, verb `publish`) in place of the promotion. Right: it is the 2026-11-26 note's own refusal, asked over the union of the active rows' and the drafts' bindings as the draft save asks it, thrown below the `_lock` gate with the door's other address refusals and before the draft is read. With one enabled holder the judgment returns nothing, so the adoption (`key` null, `into` the enabled package) is unmoved.
- **Per-item rollback naming no package** (`rollbackMetaItemUnaudited`): narrower by one cell. Where `request.packageId` is undefined, the resolved binding is null and a package-unbound active row is stored, the same `409` (verb `rollback`) answers before `restoreVersion`. Right, and placed after the ADR-0146 D11 close and the named-base close, so both `403` answers keep their order.
- **`packagelessHolderRefusal`**: new trailing parameter `arms`, default `'all'`. Right: the four existing call sites (`protocol-save.ts` 861, 882, 968; `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` 776) pass no fifth argument and none passes verb `publish` or `rollback`, so the added `arms === 'all' && verb !== 'rollback'` conjunct is true for each of them and their answers are unchanged.
- **Public surface**: `DisabledHoldersWriteVerb` is a new exported type, and the verb union of `disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal`, `disabledHoldersCustomizationRefusal` and `packagelessHolderRefusal` widens from two members to four. Right: additive. `verb !== 'delete'` selects "Nothing was written." for the two new verbs, which is true of both.
- **Tests**: five new cases in one `describe` (two publish refusals by `it.each`, the rollback refusal, two controls). The three refusal pins assert status, code, the sentence's first words, that no package is named, every stored row of the name unchanged, then the re-enable. Right for the cell they name.
- **Migration entry**: its `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` now name the two doors, and the acceptance parenthetical bounds them correctly. Its `reason` does not: see S1.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION** of `.changeset/37499-disabled-holder-unbound-row-bare-write-refused.md`, one sentence.
  Before: "there only the draft discard moves, from `200` to the `409` above."
  After: "there only the draft discard moves: over a stored package-less draft from `200` to the `409` above, and over a stored package-less row with no draft from the `409` with the `?package=` sentence to the same `409` with the enable sentence."
  Judged against the tree: **true, confirmed**. In `deleteMetaItemUnaudited` the draft discard reads the draft rows as its address and, where a package-unbound draft or active row is stored, passes `unbound: rowsAtAddress.unbound, customized: active.unbound`. With a package-less row and no draft that is `unbound: false, customized: true`, which answers `disabledHoldersCustomizationRefusal` (the enable sentence). Without the `customized` arm the same cell falls to `disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal` (the `?package=` sentence), which is the `409` it answered before #37584, as card comment 7199079202 (N11) records. The "before" sentence was false for that cell; the "after" sentence names both cells and no third one moves. The `Check Changeset` red on this head is this note and nothing else (see ②).

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37608-disabled-holder-publish-rollback-refused.md` declares `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor` and `@objectstack/spec: minor`, with a `!` title and a **BREAKING** paragraph. It matches what the diff publishes: a refusal where two doors answered `200`, and a reworded migration entry in spec. It is the level of the twin note of #37499 on `main`.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are on the PR body and the changeset, and agree with the amended claim 7212050411. Correct for the diff.
- `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered disabled-holder-package-less-row-bare-write-refused)`: the entry exists on the merge base and this diff extends it. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it as carrying a disposition, inside the `Check Changeset` job log.
- Check-runs: 73, all completed. 58 success, 13 skipped, 2 failure. Both failures are `Check Changeset` (jobs 140332765300 and 140359973930), and in both the only failing step is `check-empty-changeset --base`, on `.changeset/37499-disabled-holder-unbound-row-bare-write-refused.md` alone, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. This record is its confirmation (① above). `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Test Core` 1 to 10, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` 1 (keep `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` or drop the arm): answered, keep. The claim was amended to that spelling (7212050411) and the diff is a narrowing.
- `open_questions` 2 (should the enable `409` answer before the D11 close's `403` over an every-holder-disabled base): answered, the order is left as it is in this PR, and the diff does leave it. Changing it moves a shipped answer and is the seat's decision route (card comment 7196921497); escalated to the seat, not owed by this head.
- Dev flag, ADR-0150 D3 note left unedited (Tier H), carrier #37245: accepted, with the condition in S1. The bullet that replaces "Not judged yet" must not state the universal while the two cells of S1 stand.
- Dev flag, `reassignOrphanedMetadata` lead not measured, carrier "the seat": escalated. It has no card number; the seat owes one.
- Dev flag, N12 belongs to the seat's decision card: accepted, not this diff.
- SQL push-down: no finding. Each door adds one `packagelessAddress` read, an equality `where` on `sys_metadata` pushed to the store, and only inside the guarded cell (no package named, package-less draft or binding). No id materialisation, no in-app join. The judgment itself reads the registry in memory.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published contract on `main`: ADR-0150 D3's 2026-11-26 note says a package-less row at a name a package holds hides with its holder, and names these two doors as "not judged yet". The diff takes no declared capability away at a consumer. It makes that note's refusal real at the two doors, with the same code, the same sentence and the enable as the remedy, and a re-enable serves the stored row unchanged. Attempts to break it, by reading `packagelessDraftAddress` for every `key` and `into` pair, the D11 ordering on both doors, the enabled-holder and mixed-holder cells, and the action type's environment-own draft, found the guarded cell correct. One gap in what the narrowing covers, and three nits.

S1 (should-fix) — two writes naming no package still land on a hidden item, and the migration entry says otherwise. The diff asks only the judgment's second state (a package-unbound row or draft stored). The first state, `disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal`, which the save, the draft save, the delete and the draft discard all answer, is not asked by either door:
  - **Publish of the disabled package's own draft.** A draft saved under `?package=PKG`, the package then disabled, `POST /meta/TYPE/NAME/publish` with no `?package=`: `packagelessDraftAddress` answers `key` and `into` PKG, the new guard skips it, and the draft is promoted into the disabled package's active row. The new control test pins this as `success: true`. The bare save into that same row is refused `409` on `main`.
  - **Rollback with no package-less row stored.** A package-less row saved and later deleted leaves its history. With every holder disabled, a rollback naming no package resolves a null binding, `active.unbound` is false so the judgment is not asked, and `restoreVersion` with `packageId: null` and no active row inserts a new package-unbound row (its own docblock: "creating that package's row again when it is gone"). Read in the code, not run. The bare save in that cell is refused `409` on `main`.
  Both are listed under "Not moved" in the new changeset, so the release note is honest. Two things are not. The card's third Expected bullet ("every write naming no package" holds once this lands) is not met. And the entry's `reason`, in published spec, now reads over six writes: "They now judge the name's holders past a stored package-less row, as they already did with none stored", and "a name only disabled packages hold with no package-less row stored (its refusal keeps the ?package= remedy)". Neither is true of the publish or the rollback, which judged no holder with none stored and still do not.
  Fix, either one: ask the judgment in those two cells as well (a moved shipped answer, so through the seat's decision route if the seat reads it as beyond the ruling); or keep the cells, file the decision card that carries them, name that card in the changeset's "Not moved" paragraph, and reword the two `reason` sentences so they claim the first state only for the four earlier writes. The entry is not a prose face, so either fix moves the head and earns a delta review.

N1 (nit) — an in-process `publishMetaItem` with `packageId: null` present takes the `'packageId' in request` branch and is not asked the judgment, while `environmentActionPublishSlotRefusal` a few lines below is asked for both spellings. No product caller reaches it: the REST route spreads `packageId` only when `?package=` is set, and `publishPackageDrafts` names its package. Follow-up card or accepted deviation.

N2 (nit) — two conditions that cannot be false today. In the publish guard, `active.unbound || address.drafts.unbound` is always true once `address.kind === 'draft'` and `key` is null (and `into` null implies `key` null). In `packagelessHolderRefusal`, `verb !== 'rollback'` is never reached with `arms === 'all'`. Both are harmless; no behaviour depends on them.

N3 (nit) — the adoption cell (a package-less draft beside the disabled package's own active row, `key` null and `into` the package) is refused by this diff and is pinned by no test, and the changeset's bullet describes its "before" as a promotion "into the hidden package-less row" where it was a promotion into the package's row. The changeset is a prose face; the pin is a follow-up.

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head.
